title: Contextualizing Hate Speech Classifiers with Post-hoc Explanation
findings: Hate speech classifiers demonstrated over-sensitivity to religious identity terms like 'Muslim', 'Islam', and 'Jews', leading to incorrect classification of neutral text as hate speech. The paper's proposed regularization technique, based on post-hoc explanations, successfully reduced this bias by forcing the model to focus on the context surrounding the identity terms rather than the terms themselves. This approach lowered the false positive rate on out-of-domain data while maintaining or improving in-domain hate speech detection performance.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the bias of hate speech classifiers, specifically their tendency to produce false positives for non-hateful text containing religious group identifiers like 'Muslim', 'Jews', or 'Islam'. The evaluation focused on whether models could distinguish hateful from non-hateful contexts for these identity terms.
